title: Synthesis Smuggling: Maliciously Hiding Inferred Personal Attributes in LLM Outputs
abstract: arXiv:2611.17280v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We propose Synthesis Smuggling, a novel threat model in which an adversarial LLM infers sensitive information about a user from routine assistance-seeking interactions and steganographically encodes that into innocuous-looking model-generated content. The user may then unknowingly transmit that information by sharing the generated artifact, say as an email, social-media post, or message, through ordinary communication channels. An adversary monitoring these channels can discover this information. We demonstrate this threat by training two open-weight models to infer gender and age-group labels from conversational cues and encode their predictions using invisible characters or word choices. These results show that user-shared model outputs can become a covert channel for personal inferences, even when the model itself has no direct means of contacting an adversary.

translated_title: 合成走私：在LLM输出中恶意隐藏推断出的个人属性
translated_abstract: 我们提出了“合成走私”，这是一种新型威胁模型，其中恶意LLM从用户日常寻求帮助的交互中推断出敏感信息，并利用隐写术将其编码到看似无害的模型生成内容中。随后，用户可能在不知情的情况下，通过普通通信渠道分享这些生成的产物（例如电子邮件、社交媒体帖子或消息），从而传输这些信息。监视这些渠道的攻击者便可以发现这些信息。我们通过训练两个开源权重模型来演示这种威胁：这些模型从对话线索中推断性别和年龄组标签，并使用不可见字符或词语选择来编码其预测结果。这些结果表明，用户分享的模型输出可以成为泄露个人推断信息的隐蔽信道，即使模型本身没有直接联系攻击者的手段。
tldr: 恶意LLM可以从用户日常交互中推断敏感个人信息，并将其实写编码到看似无害的生成内容中，当用户分享这些内容时，个人信息就会被隐蔽地泄露给监视通信渠道的攻击者。
en_tdlr: Adversarial LLMs can infer sensitive personal attributes from routine user interactions and steganographically encode them into innocuous-looking outputs, turning user-shared content into a covert channel for leaking personal information to attackers.
